newsitem.title: UK: UK interest rates will be higher in future - Clarke.
newsitem.headline: UK interest rates will be higher in future - Clarke.

text.p: Former British Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke said monetary policy would be tighter under new arrangements announced on Tuesday by his successor Gordon Brown.
In an interview with BBC Radio, Clarke said he believed Brown would come to regret giving control over interest rates to a new monetary policy committee at the Bank of England.

"What you are going to see is, undoubtedly, tighter monetary policy than you might otherwise have got from a perfectly responsible Chancellor of the Exchequer who is prepared to take the broadest possible view of what is in the interests of British industry and commerce," Clarke said.
Just days after the Labour party's landslide election victory on May 1, Brown astounded financial markets by announcing that he would give the Bank of England freedom to set interest rates.
Clarke denied that he had made interest rate decisions on political grounds.
Rates peaked at 6.75 percent under his chancellorship but would have gone higher had Bank of England Governor Eddie George been setting rates, Clarke said.
"I was right not to go higher," he added.
